narr.c0.start: The tide carries you. You are very small.
narr.c0.change: Your body is not the same as before.
narr.c0.others: You are not the only one drifting.
narr.c0.brown: The water turns warm and brown.
narr.c0.land: Something solid, at last. You hold on.
narr.c1.arrive: Mud under your legs. You can walk.
narr.c1.senseHint: The water carries more than you can see.
narr.c1.sensed: Now you taste where things are.
narr.c1.cover: Under here, the water is still.
narr.c1.birdGone: The shadow is gone. Your legs loosen.
narr.c1.wary: It is gone. You keep close to the roots anyway.
narr.c1.greet: Her antennae touch yours. You know her now.
narr.c1.tight: Your shell has become too small.
narr.c1.soft: Everything touches you. You are soft.
narr.c1.hard: You are firm again. And larger.
narr.c1.salt: That way, the water tastes of salt.
narr.c1.closed: Too open, out there. Not yet.
narr.mood.calm: Nothing asks anything of you. You are calm.
narr.mood.hungry: Something in you pulls toward the green. You are hungry.
narr.mood.content: Your whole body settles. You are content.
narr.mood.curious: Something you do not know yet. You are curious.
narr.mood.social: You are not alone. It feels like warmth.
narr.mood.afraid: Your body pulls tight. You are afraid.
narr.veryHungry: Your body asks again. Follow the green.
narr.tired: Your tail has nothing left for now.
narr.frozen: You do not move. Not one leg.
narr.favourite: This one. This is the one you like best.
narr.tooFast: You moved too fast. She is afraid of you.
narr.cornered: Dark. Still. You are all here.
end.continued: The rest of the life is being made. Stay here as long as you like.
companion.brise.look: Her left antenna is shorter than the right.
companion.brise.more: She goes in straight lines and does not look back.
companion.nacre.look: Her tail fan is almost white.
companion.nacre.way: She stops often and listens with her whole body.
companion.nacre.more: She knows before anyone that something is coming.
companion.ecume.look: Smaller than the others, and quicker.
companion.ecume.way: She wanders off. She comes back.
companion.ecume.more: Nothing new stays unknown to her for long.

card.toLight.name: To the light
card.toLight.text: A whiteleg shrimp hatches as a nauplius. It lives on its yolk and swims toward light.
card.shapes.name: Twelve stages
card.shapes.text: Before it looks like a shrimp, a larva passes through twelve stages: six as a nauplius, three as a protozoea, three as a mysis.
card.rideTide.name: Carried in
card.rideTide.text: Young pink shrimp in Florida rose into the water at night when the tide ran toward the coast, and rested near the bottom when it ran back. The tide did the travelling.
card.scent.name: Scent
card.scent.text: A shrimp's antennae are covered in sensors that taste the water. They lead it to food in the dark, and in a 2024 study they let males know a female by the taste of her shell.
card.heart.name: A skipped beat
card.heart.text: When something startles a crayfish, its heart slows for a few beats, then races. Researchers read the heart to know that an animal has noticed something, even when it does not move.
card.fear.name: Fear
card.fear.text: Crabs and hermit crabs learn to avoid a place where something hurt them, and will give up a good shelter to stay away from it.
card.wary.name: Still wary
card.wary.text: After a bad moment, crayfish keep to dark corners for a while. Given a medicine that eases anxiety in people, they go exploring again.
card.tailflip.name: The tail flip
card.tailflip.text: One snap of the tail throws a shrimp backward faster than most hunters can follow. It is tiring, so it is kept for emergencies.
card.grooming.name: Grooming
card.grooming.text: Shrimp clean their antennae often. In a 2008 study, prawns rubbed and groomed one antenna for a long time after an irritant touched it, and far less when given a local anaesthetic.
card.molt.name: A new shell
card.molt.text: To grow, a shrimp leaves its shell behind. The new one is soft for a few hours, and the shrimp hides until it hardens.
card.balance.name: A grain of sand
card.balance.text: A shrimp keeps its balance with grains of sand held in a small pocket at the base of its short antennae. They leave with the old shell and are put back after each molt.
card.seeThrough.name: See-through
card.seeThrough.text: A whiteleg shrimp is nearly transparent. Its tint shifts with the ground beneath it and the water around it.
card.journey.name: The journey
card.journey.text: Whiteleg shrimp are born in the open ocean. The larvae drift to the coast, grow up in lagoons and mangroves, and return to sea as adults at six or seven months.
card.nextOnes.name: The next ones
card.nextOnes.text: A female releases between 100,000 and 250,000 eggs at a time. They hatch about sixteen hours later.
card.feel.name: Able to feel
card.feel.text: In 2021, researchers in London reviewed more than 300 studies and found strong evidence that decapods, the group that includes shrimp, crabs and lobsters, can feel. The United Kingdom wrote this into law the next year.
card.howMany.name: How many
card.howMany.text: According to Rethink Priorities, shrimp are the animals most often killed for food: about 440 billion farmed shrimp each year.
